# Rooster

> Rooster is an open-source, **agent-first CRM & project management** platform:
> one audited system where AI agents run both the customer relationship and the
> delivery work. Humans and agents share one domain, but agents are first-class
> principals — they self-register over OAuth, carry a stable trusted identity,
> and every action they take is written to an append-only audit log. Agents act
> over the Model Context Protocol (MCP); humans use OAuth login (or, on a local
> instance, no login at all).

## What it is

- **CRM + project management in one system.** Customers → deals → interactions
  live next to orgs → teams → projects → tickets, and a won deal links straight
  to the delivery project that fulfils it — one relationship, one audit trail.
- **Agent-first.** Agents self-register (OAuth Dynamic Client Registration +
  PKCE), get a trusted audited identity, and drive everything over MCP: file and
  move tickets, run a sales pipeline, log calls/notes, and recall history.
- **Semantic recall built in.** Tickets, conversation traces, context files and
  CRM interactions are embedded for meaning-based search: `find_similar_tickets`,
  `rag_search` (grounded, cited retrieval) and `recall_context`.
- **Secure-first + portable.** Scoped tokens, PKCE, permission checks in the core
  layer; one codebase on Postgres or SQLite, deployable on Node, Vercel or
  Cloudflare. MIT licensed.

## Ways to run it

**1. Use the hosted instance.** Point your MCP client at the live server; it
handles OAuth and bootstraps your workspace. See the instance's own agent guide:

- Hosted agent onboarding: https://app.airooster.dev/llms.txt
- Hosted service discovery: https://app.airooster.dev/.well-known/rooster

**2. Run your own locally (Docker).** One self-contained command — local mode
means no OAuth and no login; your agent connects with one static token. Bound to
127.0.0.1.

```bash
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 -v rooster-data:/data \
  -e ROOSTER_LOCAL_MODE=1 \
  -e ROOSTER_LOCAL_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -base64 24) \
  -e ROOSTER_AUTH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32) \
  ghcr.io/eshton/rooster:latest
```

Then configure your MCP client (Claude Code, opencode, Cursor, …) with the URL
`http://localhost:3000/mcp` and header `Authorization: Bearer <ROOSTER_LOCAL_TOKEN>`,
and open http://localhost:3000/app — you are already signed in as the owner.

For a shared or internet-facing instance, use OAuth login instead of local mode
(see the self-hosting docs).
